options: Flagging a record as deleted without physically removing it from storage
Permanently overwriting the underlying storage so data is unrecoverable
A type of encryption applied before deletion
A legal term for an erasure request that was denied
questions.explain: A soft delete sets a flag like is_deleted = true. The row is still physically present and still readable by anyone with direct database or backup access.

questions.q: Under GDPR Article 17, which of these is a legitimate ground for an organization to decline an erasure request?
options: A legal obligation requires the organization to keep the data for a defined retention period
The organization simply prefers to keep the data
The data is more than one year old
The individual has previously made an access request
questions.explain: Article 17 lists specific exceptions, including compliance with a legal retention obligation, exercising freedom of expression, public-interest archiving, and establishing or defending legal claims.

questions.q: Why doesn't deleting a customer's account typically remove their data from a nightly backup taken the day before?
options: Because the backup is a separate snapshot taken before the deletion occurred, and most backups can't be selectively edited
Because backups are always encrypted and therefore exempt from erasure rules
Because backups only ever contain non-personal data
Because deleting an account automatically triggers deletion from all backups
questions.explain: A backup captured before the deletion still physically contains the data; organizations typically document that it will age out when that backup's own retention period expires rather than editing old backups directly.

questions.q: What distinguishes 'secure deletion' from a basic hard delete?
options: Secure deletion ensures the underlying storage is actually unrecoverable, such as through overwriting or destroying the encryption key
Secure deletion only applies to soft-deleted records
Secure deletion is a synonym for hard delete with no practical difference
Secure deletion means the data is moved to a different database instead of removed
questions.explain: A hard delete removes the row from the active table, but remnants can remain on disk. Secure deletion goes further to make the data unrecoverable from storage media as well.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the 'hard 90%' of fulfilling an erasure request?
options: Finding and addressing every other place the data landed — backups, caches, logs, and third-party processors
Writing the SQL statement that deletes the row from the primary table
Getting written approval from the data subject before deleting anything
Classifying the data before it can be deleted
questions.explain: Marking a row deleted in production is described as the easy 10%; the hard part is locating and addressing every other copy of that data across backups, caches, logs, and any third party it was shared with.
